title: Term Life Insurance: Number of Policies per Owner
content:
**Contract provision — Term Life Insurance.** An owner may hold any number of Ashgrove term policies, on the owner's own life or on other lives in which the owner has an insurable interest. The count of policies is not capped; there is no maximum number of term policies per customer.

What is capped is the total face amount on one insured life, under the per-insured aggregate face limit of Term Life Insurance — not the number of policies an owner holds.

| Question | Answer under this provision |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many term policies one owner holds? | No |
| May an owner hold a policy on another person's life? | Yes, where the owner has an insurable interest in that life |
| What is limited instead? | The total face amount on one insured |

Hypothetical: an owner holding three term policies — one on the owner's own life and two on the life of a spouse — is not stopped from a fourth by the count of policies.
